track.subject: Reading
track.description: Thirteen full-year planning skeletons connect foundational word reading, literature, information, and disciplinary reading through a coherent progression of evidence and text complexity.
track.scopeNote: Original instructional outlines aligned to the 2010 Common Core reading standards: RL and RI in K–8 and the 9–10/11–12 bands; RF K–5 including lettered subskills; RH and RST in the 6–8, 9–10, and 11–12 bands. All these applicable reading standards are mapped; numbered standard 8 is not applicable in RL at any grade or band. Anchor reading standards are represented through their grade/band implementations rather than a duplicate registry. This is reading scope, not complete English language arts, official endorsement, a delivered text collection, or evidence of learner mastery. The 36-week pacing, text choices, phonics order, and annual subdivision of bands are editorial. Schools select accessible, age-appropriate, legally available texts and coordinate disciplinary reading; tasks and summaries here are original.

courses.title: Kindergarten Reading
courses.scopeNote: A 36-week reading skeleton, not a supplied lesson library or a full ELA course. Literature and informational reading recur throughout; writing and discussion show reading understanding but do not claim coverage of W, SL, or L standards. RL standard 8 is not applicable to literature and is intentionally absent. Includes the grade’s RF standards and lettered subskills; systematic word-work order is an editorial sequence, adjusted through observation.
prerequisites: No independent reading prerequisite; begin with conversation, listening, play, and a brief observation of print and sound awareness.
outcomes: Retell a familiar story with support.
Retell a topic and details with support.
Participate purposefully in group literature reading.
Participate purposefully in group information reading.
Apply the grade’s foundational word-reading skills in fresh words and connected text, with comprehension and appropriate fluency.
courses.nextStep: Continue to ccss-reading-1; use the final conference to identify specific foundations or text demands needing support.
courses.yearBridge: Children begin by handling books, hearing word parts, and noticing details in shared stories and information books. Retelling and discussion then connect events, vocabulary, author and illustrator roles, pictures, and reasons before children compare familiar books. Alongside that oral comprehension work, cumulative letter–sound instruction leads into short emergent texts and a final conference that records listening comprehension and decoding separately.
courses.crossSubject: Use order words, sorting, and one-to-one picture counts to clarify text details; oral reasoning and pointing remain valid responses.
routines: Read literature and information every week; build knowledge and vocabulary across connected texts while also allowing wide, self-selected reading.
Use rich daily read-alouds and supported conversation for comprehension; choose independent decoding texts for taught correspondences. Record listening and word-reading evidence separately.

Teach the foundational sequence explicitly and cumulatively in short daily sessions; select practice from observed needs, and revisit earlier patterns across every unit. Context confirms a decoded word and supports self-correction; do not teach guessing words from pictures.
Use oral explanations, drawings, annotation, and short written responses as appropriate; assess the reading reasoning separately from handwriting or extended composition.
Choose age-appropriate texts with qualitative complexity, vocabulary/syntax, background knowledge, and reader/task demands in view; no single readability score determines access or placement.
Revisit earlier phonics and comprehension checks during every unit and use results to select the next small-group lesson.
